definition.interpretation: The experiment returned a preference stability delta of 0.25, which technically met the threshold of 0.2; however, the lack of a comparative control group (i.e., an agent operating without the episodic memory buffer) makes it impossible to attribute this stability to the memory component versus baseline architectural performance.
definition.limitations: The single-agent design failed to isolate the causal mechanism of memory. The environment lacked controlled perturbations to stress-test preference stability.
definition.next_step: Design and execute a comparative experimental protocol that introduces a control condition: a standard reinforcement learning agent without episodic memory access.

definition.reason: Previous inconclusive results necessitate a controlled comparative study to validate if memory buffers actually confer stability compared to memory-less baselines.
definition.stop: Completion of comparative stable-vs-baseline metric analysis.
definition.uncertainty: Whether baseline architectural noise in current simulation environments masks the stabilizing effect of episodic memory.

proposal.summary: Synthesized the inconclusive findings from the initial memory stability experiment, identified the lack of a control group as the primary limitation, and prioritized a comparative experimental design for the next iteration.
proposal.title: Interpreting Memory-Based Preference Stability Results
